name: Startup funding rounds → exit
description: An absorbing funnel. A company progresses through funding rounds until it reaches an exit — IPO, acquisition, acquihire or shutdown. Each round conditions its size, the size conditions dilution, and dilution conditions founder ownership.

states.label: Seed
states.notes:
First institutional money in.

The graduation rate to Series A is the most contested number in this whole model. Published figures vary widely — cohort definition, vintage, and whether "still private and alive" counts as a failure all move it by tens of percent.

The 0.35 here is a placeholder. Substitute a rate from a cohort you trust and re-run.

states.label: Series A
states.notes: Product-market fit is the implicit gate. Attrition from here is still heavy but less brutal than at seed.

states.label: Series B
states.notes: Scaling capital. Companies reaching B have materially higher survival odds, and acquisition becomes a more common exit than shutdown.

states.label: Series C+
states.notes: Late stage. Modelled as a single absorbing-ish stage rather than separate C/D/E rounds — collapsing them keeps the diagram readable without changing the exit distribution much.

states.label: IPO
states.notes: Public listing. The rarest terminal state by a wide margin.

states.label: Acquisition
states.notes:
Trade sale at a price that returns capital and pays the founders.

Counted as a success here, but note this lumps together a 3x and a 30x outcome. If that distinction matters to you, split it into two terminal states in the JSON.

states.label: Acquihire
states.notes: Team absorbed, product wound down. Classified as a failure because the preference stack usually leaves common shareholders with little or nothing, even though it does not look like a shutdown from the outside.

states.label: Shutdown
states.notes: Wind-down. The single most likely terminal state for a company entering at seed.

seed.notes: Seed-to-A graduation. See the note on the Seed node — this is the number to argue with first.

seriesC.notes: Conditional on reaching late stage. Unconditionally it compounds to about 1.3% of seed-stage companies (0.35 × 0.45 × 0.42 × 0.18) — check it against the run counts in the Outcomes view after a simulation.

variables.label: Round size
variables.notes: Capital raised at this stage. Terminal states raise nothing, so they put all their mass on the zero-width "none" level.

variables.label: Dilution
variables.notes:
Equity sold in this round, conditioned on its size.

Larger rounds dilute more in absolute terms but the relationship flattens at the top, because mega-rounds are usually priced off a much higher valuation.

variables.label: Founder ownership
variables.notes:
Combined founder stake after this round.

Caveat worth knowing before you read too much into it: this conditions only on the current round's dilution, not on the cumulative history, because a variable in this engine has exactly one parent. It therefore understates the compounding of dilution across many rounds. Reading it as "ownership typical of a company at this stage" is fair; reading it as a running cap-table balance is not.

outcomes.label: Exit outcome
outcomes.notes: The terminal state the company landed on.

outcomes.label: Success vs failure
outcomes.notes: IPO and acquisition count as success; acquihire and shutdown as failure.
